consideredAndDeclined.whyDeclined: Three reasons, and I record them so the choice is auditable rather than silent. First, that clause is not introduced by this act — it is pre-existing text written when D-135 added the row, and the act's discipline is to change only the stale 'no contract exists' clause. Second, D-138's owed act is narrowly scoped to recording the accepted candidate while keeping the row OPEN, Class A unopened and not SATISFIED; adding a leftover inventory to the cell would exceed the authority the entry is exercising. Third, D-139's L section deliberately keeps the leftover inventory in the coordinator decisions rather than the register. Raising it now would also leave the just-adopted DR-133 cell asymmetric. If the coordinator wants remainders in-cell, that is its own decision covering both rows, not a repair to this one.

Adding a fourth requirement now, after the entry delivered exactly what I specified, would be moving the goalposts.

coordinatorSummary: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Fourteen attacks run, one landed and it is advisory-grade. Custody is clean and the control instruments are single this turn: subject 956d2d37 at 0444 unmoved, one dispatch and one prompt agreeing on the pin, HEAD never left cb6d10e, file 08 at 59b8e8a3 and COORD at 2b5a7c6a with a clean tree. Because file 08 moved under this entry's feet when D-140 was applied, I audited the predecessor's application before trusting the premises: cb6d10e changed exactly one file-08 line, and the resulting DR-133 cell equals the bytes both reviewers consented to at D-140 turn 2, with DR-131 untouched and the 4-of-32 snapshot intact. On that base the entry holds under every attack. The before-cell is byte-exact against the live DR-131 row, located by a prefix that matches exactly one line. The after-cell carries all three load-bearing parts of the register's established candidate form, the link resolves from file 08's directory to a file that exists, that file hashes to exactly the 64-hex digest written beside it, no pipe can split the row, the leading label and both trailing sentences are byte-identical to the before-cell, and normalising for the decision id, artifact and digest, the proposed cell is the same string as the DR-133 cell now live — so the register stays internally consistent across the pair. The authority citation resolves rather than dangling: D-138's entry pins its subject at c609de64, which equals the live turn-2 draft, and that subject's numbered item 6 is the owed-later-work item; the same holds for D-136 and D-140. The act is scoped exactly to what D-138 owed and is the single dedicated H2 cycle that my D-140 SF-2 and Codex's MF-1 produced, and Decision item 2 goes further than its sibling by restating D-138's own finding that recording v2 still does not make DR-131 eligible in kind. The advisory is that the COORD-scope refusal dropped in the D-140 rewrite is still absent here; nothing becomes permitted, since COORD changes are decisions and H3 is refused by name twice, but the clause is worth restoring in both entries. I also record one thing I considered and declined: the DR-105 and DR-114 precedent cells name what remains before SATISFIED, and this cell does not name DR-131's NT-1..NT-8 leftover. I am not raising it, because that clause is pre-existing text this act must not touch, D-138's owed act is scoped to the candidate recording alone, D-139 deliberately keeps leftover inventories in the decisions rather than the register, and I specified the form's requirements in D-140 and should not add a fourth after the entry delivered them. After this entry only H3 and the L-section leftover closures remain owed.
